title: Mountains and Volcanoes (KS2)
subject: Geography
strapline: How mountains and volcanoes form, and what erupts.
facts: The Earth's surface is split into huge pieces called tectonic plates that move very slowly.
Fold mountains form when two plates push together and crumple the land upwards over millions of years.
A volcano is an opening in the Earth's crust where molten rock reaches the surface.
Molten rock underground is called magma; once it erupts onto the surface it is called lava.
When a volcano erupts it can throw out lava, ash and gases.
Volcanoes and earthquakes often happen at the edges of tectonic plates.
A dormant volcano could erupt again; an extinct one is not expected to.

quick_quiz.q: What are the huge moving pieces of the Earth's surface called?
What is molten rock called once it reaches the surface?

quick_quiz.a: two plates push together and crumple the land upwards

teacher_tips: Use a plate-boundary map to show why volcanoes cluster where they do.
Keep magma (underground) vs lava (surface) crisp — a classic mix-up.
Link to real, recent eruptions to show geography is live, not history.
